name: Customer Complaint Handling
orchestration_notes: Customer submits complaint via a channel (web, mobile, branch, phone). CAP-001 (Retail Banking) creates the ComplaintCase and owns the resolution lifecycle. CAP-005 (Compliance & Regulatory) consumes complaint events for FCA DISP reporting obligations. No capability calls another capability's API directly — all cross-capability coordination is via events on the Event Bus.

regulatory_basis.legislation: FCA Handbook — DISP (Dispute Resolution: Complaints sourcebook)
sections: DISP 1.6 — Time limits for resolving complaints
regulatory_basis.obligation: The bank must acknowledge complaints promptly, resolve them within 3 business days (Summary Resolution Communication) or 8 weeks (Final Response), and report complaint volumes to the FCA half-yearly (DISP 1.10).

sections: PRIN 12 — Act to deliver good outcomes
regulatory_basis.obligation: Complaint handling is a Consumer Support outcome obligation. Root cause analysis must be applied to complaint patterns to identify systemic conduct issues.

sections: DISP 3 — Complaint resolution by the FOS
regulatory_basis.obligation: The bank must cooperate with FOS investigations. Customers must be informed of their right to refer to the FOS in the Final Response or 8-week letter.

phases.name: Complaint Receipt and Acknowledgement
phases.description: Customer submits a complaint through a channel (web portal, mobile app, branch, phone, or written letter). The channel records the complaint details and creates a ComplaintCase with status = received. SVC-001 (Retail Banking Core) acknowledges receipt to the customer within 1 business day. A complaint reference number is issued. SVC-015 (Compliance Core) is notified via ComplaintReceived event for regulatory tracking.
persona_actions: Customer selects 'Make a Complaint' or equivalent entry point in the channel
Customer provides complaint subject, description, affected product/account, and desired outcome
Customer receives acknowledgement with reference number and expected resolution timeline
system_actions: Channel collects complaint details: subject, description, affected_product_id, affected_account_id, desired_outcome
Channel calls SVC-001 POST /complaints to create ComplaintCase with status = received
SVC-001 assigns complaint_reference (unique identifier), records channel, timestamps receipt
SVC-001 publishes ComplaintReceived (EVT-138)

SVC-001 dispatches acknowledgement notification to customer via SVC-053 (Notifications): reference number, receipt timestamp, regulatory timeline (3 business days for summary resolution or 8 weeks for final response)
SVC-015 consumes ComplaintReceived for DISP regulatory reporting counter
phases.exit_condition: ComplaintCase created with status = received; ComplaintReceived published; acknowledgement dispatched to customer

phases.name: Complaint Triage and Assignment
phases.description: Customer Service Agent (PER-062) reviews the complaint and categorises it by product, complaint type, and initial severity. The complaint is assigned to the appropriate resolution owner. Complex or regulated complaints (e.g. involving fraud, PPI, mortgage conduct) are escalated to a specialist team. A target resolution date is set based on complexity.
persona_actions: PER-062 reviews complaint details and customer account history
PER-062 categorises complaint: product_type, complaint_type (conduct / service / product / fraud), severity (low / medium / high)
PER-062 assigns complaint to resolution owner (self, specialist, or escalation queue)
PER-062 sets target_resolution_date based on complexity (3 business days for simple, 8 weeks maximum)
system_actions: SVC-001 presents ComplaintCase to PER-062 via internal portal
PER-062 updates ComplaintCase: category, complaint_type, severity, assigned_to, target_resolution_date
SVC-001 updates ComplaintCase status = in_triage
SVC-001 publishes ComplaintTriaged (EVT-139)
If severity = high or complaint_type = regulated: SVC-001 flags ComplaintCase for compliance oversight; SVC-015 consumes ComplaintTriaged to apply enhanced monitoring
phases.exit_condition: ComplaintCase status = triaged; resolution owner assigned; target resolution date set
nfr_references: Triage complete within 4 business hours of receipt

phases.name: Investigation and Resolution
phases.description: Resolution owner investigates the complaint. This may involve reviewing account history, transaction records, call recordings, product terms, and any applicable regulatory rules. The resolution owner determines whether the complaint is upheld, partially upheld, or rejected, and drafts the resolution response. Redress calculations are performed if financial compensation is warranted.
persona_actions: PER-062 reviews account history, transactions, and any prior complaint records
PER-062 consults relevant product terms and governance rules
PER-062 determines outcome: upheld / partially_upheld / rejected
PER-062 calculates redress amount if applicable (financial compensation, service remedy)
PER-062 drafts resolution response for customer
system_actions: SVC-001 presents customer account history and transaction records to PER-062
PER-062 updates ComplaintCase: investigation_notes, outcome, redress_amount, response_draft
If outcome = upheld and redress_amount > 0: SVC-001 initiates redress payment instruction via SVC-009 (Domestic Payments)
SVC-001 updates ComplaintCase status = resolved (pending communication)
SVC-001 publishes ComplaintResolved (EVT-140) with outcome and redress_amount
SVC-015 consumes ComplaintResolved for DISP outcome reporting
phases.exit_condition: Complaint outcome determined; ComplaintCase status = resolved; redress payment initiated if applicable
nfr_references: Resolution within 3 business days (Summary Resolution — DISP 1.6.2R)

phases.name: Response Communication and Closure
phases.description: Customer receives the resolution decision via their preferred channel. For complaints resolved within 3 business days, a Summary Resolution Communication (SRC) is issued. For more complex complaints resolved after 3 days, a Final Response Letter is required containing the decision, rationale, and FOS referral rights. The complaint is closed and the record retained for audit.
persona_actions: Customer receives resolution communication (SRC or Final Response Letter)
Customer accepts resolution or exercises right to refer to FOS
If customer accepts: complaint is closed
If customer refers to FOS: bank prepares FOS response pack
system_actions: SVC-001 generates resolution communication: SRC (if resolved ≤ 3 business days) or Final Response Letter (if resolved > 3 days)
Final Response Letter must include: outcome, rationale, redress details, FOS referral rights and 6-month referral window (DISP 1.6.7R)
SVC-053 dispatches communication via customer's preferred channel
SVC-001 updates ComplaintCase status = closed; records closure_timestamp
SVC-001 publishes ComplaintClosed (EVT-141)
SVC-015 consumes ComplaintClosed; updates DISP half-yearly reporting dataset
SVC-103
phases.exit_condition: Resolution communicated to customer; ComplaintCase status = closed; DISP reporting updated; audit record created
nfr_references: FOS referral rights included in Final Response

happy_path.description: Customer submits complaint via web portal. Agent triages and assigns within 4 hours. Investigation resolves the complaint within 3 business days. Summary Resolution Communication issued. Customer accepts resolution. Complaint closed. DISP reporting updated.

alternative_paths.name: Complex Complaint — Final Response Required
alternative_paths.description: Complaint cannot be resolved within 3 business days (e.g. involves regulatory investigation, third-party evidence, or multiple products). An 8-week extension letter is issued at day 5 if not resolved. Final Response Letter issued with full DISP-compliant content including FOS referral rights.
additional_steps: At day 5 if unresolved: SVC-001 dispatches 8-week update letter to customer

alternative_paths.name: Phone Channel Complaint
alternative_paths.description: Customer raises complaint by phone. PER-062 (Customer Service Agent) creates the ComplaintCase via the internal portal during the call. If the complaint is simple and resolved on the call (within 3 business days window), an SRC is issued immediately.
additional_steps: Call recording created and linked to ComplaintCase for audit trail

alternative_paths.name: Regulated Complaint — Compliance Escalation
alternative_paths.description: Complaint involves a regulated product or conduct concern (mortgage mis-selling, CONC breach, Consumer Duty outcome failure). Compliance officer (PER-052) is assigned to oversee the investigation. SVC-015 applies enhanced monitoring. Root cause analysis required as part of Consumer Duty obligations.
additional_steps: PER-052 reviews complaint for systemic conduct risk
Root cause analysis recorded in ComplaintCase.root_cause_analysis

exception_paths.name: 8-Week Deadline Breach
exception_paths.description: Complaint not resolved within 8 weeks. A Holding Response is issued to the customer with an explanation of the delay and an FOS referral right effective immediately. The delay is flagged to the Compliance team as a DISP breach. An incident record is raised.
exception_paths.trigger: ComplaintCase target_resolution_date exceeded with status != closed
exception_paths.customer_message: We apologise that we have been unable to resolve your complaint within 8 weeks. You now have the right to refer your complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service.
exception_paths.internal_action: SVC-015 raises compliance incident; FCA DISP breach recorded; PER-052 notified

exception_paths.name: FOS Referral
exception_paths.description: Customer exercises their right to refer the complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service within 6 months of the Final Response. Bank prepares an FOS Response Pack (case summary, evidence, correspondence) and cooperates with FOS investigation. ComplaintCase status updated to fos_referred.
exception_paths.trigger: Customer notifies bank of FOS referral or FOS contacts bank directly
exception_paths.internal_action: PER-062 prepares FOS Response Pack; SVC-001 updates ComplaintCase status = fos_referred; SVC-015 tracks FOS case

exception_paths.name: Redress Payment Failure
exception_paths.description: Redress payment to the customer fails (invalid account details, payment processing error). SVC-009 publishes PaymentFailed event. SVC-001 records payment failure in ComplaintCase. PER-062 is alerted to contact the customer and arrange alternative payment method. Resolution communication is not sent until redress payment is confirmed.
exception_paths.trigger: SVC-009 publishes PaymentFailed for redress_payment_id linked to ComplaintCase
exception_paths.internal_action: PER-062 alerted; alternative payment arrangement initiated; ComplaintCase status remains resolved_pending_redress

design_decisions.decision: CAP-001 (Retail Banking) owns the ComplaintCase lifecycle. CAP-005 (Compliance) participates via event consumption for DISP reporting, not by owning complaint records.
design_decisions.rationale: Complaints are a customer service and relationship management function — a Retail Banking concern. Compliance's role is regulatory reporting and oversight, not complaint resolution. Separating ownership prevents compliance from becoming a bottleneck in every complaint resolution.
alternatives_considered: Joint ownership with a shared complaint management service
design_decisions.rejected_because: Joint ownership creates ambiguous accountability. A compliance-owned system would mean every complaint, however minor, routes through a regulated function, increasing cost and latency.

design_decisions.decision: Summary Resolution Communication (SRC) is used for complaints resolved within 3 business days. Final Response Letter with FOS referral rights is required for all other resolutions.
design_decisions.rationale: This mirrors DISP 1.6 requirements exactly: the SRC is a DISP-defined mechanism for prompt resolution. Automatically generating the correct letter type based on elapsed time removes the risk of non-compliant responses.
alternatives_considered: Always issue a Final Response Letter
design_decisions.rejected_because: Always issuing Final Response Letters for simple 1-day resolutions creates unnecessary regulatory overhead and a worse customer experience.
